desc:
Rectangular buildings stand on a flat line. Building [left, right, height] occupies the horizontal range from left to right (width right - left) and is height tall. Buildings may overlap, nest or touch.

Seen from far away, the buildings form one silhouette: above every position x its height is the tallest building covering x (0 where there is none). Return the area under this silhouette, modulo 1,000,000,007.

buildings = [[2, 9, 10], [3, 7, 15], [5, 12, 12], [15, 20, 10], [19, 24, 8]]  ->  212

Heights: 10 on [2, 3), 15 on [3, 7), 12 on [7, 12), 0 on [12, 15), 10 on [15, 20) and 8 on [20, 24), so the area is 10 + 60 + 60 + 0 + 50 + 32 = 212.
constraints: buildings[i] = [left, right, height] with 0 ≤ left < right ≤ 10<sup>9</sup>
The true area can exceed 32 bits, hence the modulo
hints: Adding up the areas of the rectangles double-counts overlaps. Between two neighbouring building edges the silhouette is flat, though. How many such flat pieces are there?
Sort all distinct x-coordinates (every left and right edge). Between two consecutive coordinates the height is the maximum height of the buildings covering that strip.

Sweep left to right with a max-heap of (height, right). Push buildings whose left edge has been reached, pop the top while its right edge is already behind you, and multiply the top height by the strip width.
editorial: Let x0 < x1 < ... be the sorted distinct edge coordinates. Inside the strip [xi, xi+1) no building starts or ends, so each building either covers the whole strip or none of it, and the silhouette height is constant there.

Sweep the strips from left to right. A max-heap keyed by height stores (height, right) of the buildings that have started. At strip i, push every building with left ≤ xi and pop the top while its right ≤ xi (lazy deletion: a stale entry that is not on top cannot influence the maximum). The top height times the strip width is the contribution of the strip; empty heap means height 0.
Each building enters and leaves the heap once: O(n log n) time, O(n) space. Python integers do not overflow, so take the modulo at the end (in fixed-width languages reduce after each strip).
solution:
import heapq


def silhouetteArea(buildings):
    MOD = 1000000007
    bs = sorted(buildings)
    xs = sorted({x for l, r, h in bs for x in (l, r)})
    heap = []
    i = 0
    total = 0
    for j in range(len(xs) - 1):
        x = xs[j]
        while i < len(bs) and bs[i][0] <= x:
            heapq.heappush(heap, (-bs[i][2], bs[i][1]))
            i += 1
        while heap and heap[0][1] <= x:
            heapq.heappop(heap)
        if heap:
            total += -heap[0][0] * (xs[j + 1] - x)
    return total % MOD
